args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the deploy of checkout-api v2.3.1 to production, the service failed health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of 18%. The release candidate v2.3.1-rc had also been unhealthy in staging. Action taken: rolled checkout-api back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Checked after rollback: all regions on v2.3.0, healthy, error rate 0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause in v2.3.1 before redeploying, and look at why it was promoted even though the RC was unhealthy in staging.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and the service is healthy again. I also opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged the on-call engineer.

- **What went wrong:** after v2.3.1 was deployed, checkout-api failed health checks in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with an error rate of 18%.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. A check afterward shows all three regions on v2.3.0, healthy, with the error rate down to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 is a SEV2 for checkout-api. It describes the failure, the rollback and the check afterward. It also lists two follow-ups:
  - Find the root cause in v2.3.1 before deploying it again.
  - Find out why v2.3.1 reached production when its release candidate (v2.3.1-rc) was already unhealthy in staging.

No approval was needed, because v2.3.0 had already been healthy in production.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
